How many employees do you support in your organizations? What is the main focus of your HR departments? What are your main challenges? What are your main strengths? Share your experiences! (Please maintain anonymity for the sake of the field)

I'll start. Right now, in total, my org has tens of thousands of employees, but I support nearly 1000 (with my team). Our main focus is maintaining and preparing for future growth, training and development (with the help of our training department), and employee relations. We have dedicated benefits, payroll, data maintenance, etc departments so the the specifics of those areas are handled by the SMEs in those areas.

I love my job, plain and simple. My biggest personal challenge is finding a way to decompress from the stresses of random crazy things that happen throughout each day. I can't talk about it with anyone I work with, other than the other people in HR, and I typically like to talk through things to relieve stress and gain perspective. So right now, my goal is to find a way to get into a comfortable and proactive groove. If anyone has any pointers or advice from their own experiences, I would love to hear it!

Your turn.

I work in the temporary staffing industry. We have an average of 500 temps in the field in any given week. Our HR department (me, plus two assistants; I also oversee the receptionist) primarily handles hiring paperwork and orientation, safety and training, benefits administration, and employee relations. My boss (a VP of our parent company) handles the big picture strategic planning. We have separate departments for payroll/accounting and recruiting.

With a small staff (<20), our biggest challenge is keeping up. But I think having so few staff also makes our temporary employees feel more comfortable, and fosters genuine long-term relationships. Our temps know they're not just another face in the crowd, as they would be at a larger agency, and that they can turn to a specific person(s) if they have a question or problem. There's still craziness, but I think this minimizes a lot of the drama that our HR department might otherwise face.

Thanks for responding! Have you found a pretty good daily groove, even with the random things that come up every day? Also, is your staffing agency geared toward a particular industry or is it more general?

I work for a fairly large privately owned industrial manufacturing business. We have a little over 1500 employees and about 1100 of which are direct hires. I handle all the leave for the company as well the benefits administration for roughly half of the direct hires. We have three locations and an HR department at two with a staff totaling ten (two at one yard and eight at the other). HR at my job handles all recruiting, hiring, personnel record keeping, PTO, attendance tracking, benefits and leave administration, employee relations, etc. Our safety department (which handles orientation) and our payroll department are separate from HR.

Unfortunately, there is a lot of drama in my department and the company in general. We simply are a small company that grew too quickly. I tend to be able keep out of the drama since my job is subject to federal rules and regulations mainly and keeping up to date with them all is almost a full time job in itself. I do like what I do since I am able to help our employees when they need it most (thank you, FMLA); the benefits portion can get frustrating at times, but it's very rewarding when everything works out well.

What is the craziest, most absurd thing that has ever happened to you at a concert or festival?

At a Goldfinger show a few summers ago the singer exclaims to the crowd, "We want to see who the gnarliest person here is! Who is the guy that is going to come on stage and eat a Twinkie out of the drummer's ass?!" Surely enough, some dude rose to the opportunity. I remember the disgust of the crowd as the drummer stood on a chair, bent over, Twinkie sticking out the hairy crack as this dude takes multiple bites. After he finishes, he throws his hands up in victory and attempts a stage dive, everyone moves out of the way, he body slams the hard concrete from 5 or 6 feet off the ground. He leaves shortly after.

Was in the pit, about 2 people from the stage barrier at a Metallica concert. Suddenly something really painful is jabbed into my back. I thought maybe someone jabbed me with a lit cigarette. We were all packed in too tightly for me to turn around or figure out what was wrong.

I signaled the people around me that I wanted up and out. While I was being lifted and pushed over the people in front of me so I could get out of the area, someone pulled one of my shoes off.

So now I'm standing in the area between the barriers and the stage and I can see my shoe getting tossed around back and forth over the crowd. I had to walk up the stairs of the stadium and through the concourse with only one shoe.

I eventually got my shoe back and never figured out what was shoved into my back. No burn mark or hole in my shirt. Just a tender spot that hurt to poke at for a while

Still enjoyed the concert though
